source.title: AsymptoticNG: A regularized natural gradient optimization algorithm with look-ahead strategy
source.authors: Zedong Tang; Fenlong Jiang; Jun-Ke Song; Mao-Guo Gong; Hao Li; F. Yu; Zidong Wang; Min Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; figure labels and plots are partly garbled, and numerical values for the learning curves are not stated in prose.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer training recipes and reports validation performance, using a different optimizer comparison to examine generalization differences.
record.gate_note: Own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 validation-loss and validation-accuracy comparisons among SGD, K-FAC, truncated K-FAC, ANG, and IFANG are described. Learning-curve values are only in figures, so no precise curve numbers are extracted. Time-cost results do not measure the claim and are omitted. Cited findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study cites adaptive optimizers' generalization disadvantage as motivation but explicitly investigates a similar phenomenon in second-order natural-gradient methods. Its experiments compare SGD, K-FAC, ANG and IFANG, not the adaptive methods or recovery procedures named in V4. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ANG combines rapid early second-order convergence with later performance close to first-order optimization through a smooth transition. They present IFANG as a faster, device-friendly alternative with somewhat weaker but acceptable accuracy and loss.
record.recipe_differences: Tests K-FAC, ANG, IFANG, and SGD on CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet rather than the optimizer comparisons and benchmark suite specified in V4; figures lack readable numerical validation results.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100) and the ANG lambda strategy; authors report strategy 1 is most stable and best at suppressing overfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet, K-FAC converges rapidly early but has poorer final validation accuracy and more late overfitting than SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order natural-gradient optimization can generalize worse than SGD under the tested training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: ANG approaches first-order generalization performance smoothly after rapid early convergence; strategy 1 is reported as the most stable and best at suppressing overfitting across both datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressively blending natural and Euclidean gradient directions can improve the generalization and transition stability of natural-gradient training.

fits_no_version.finding: IFANG trades some accuracy and loss performance for reduced computation relative to the natural-gradient methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More aggressive natural-gradient approximations can reduce computation with some predictive-performance cost.

record.problems: Validation curves are only reported in figures and are garbled in the supplied text; no numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates are provided. Results are limited to ResNet on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and the optimizer comparison is not the adaptive-optimizer comparison specified in V4.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row cap. Table 1 reports optimizer computation time, not the claimed generalization behavior, so it is not included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance versus natural labels.
Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under limited tuning, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, Adam-to-SGD switching, and language-model outcomes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and their dependence on data size, configuration and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied prose supports qualitative optimizer comparisons despite unreadable plotted values. It does not justify extending V4 from adaptive gradient methods to the separately discussed second-order methods. No external sources were consulted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
The paper compares SGD with K-FAC and ANG, not the adaptive optimizers, benchmarks, or tuning conditions named in this version; its plots show validation curves without readable numerical values.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and ensuing test accuracy.
